newsitem.title: IRAQ: Turkey moves to trap Kurdish rebels in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Turkey moves to trap Kurdish rebels in Iraq.

text.p: Turkish armed forces sought to trap Kurdish guerrillas in the mountains of northern Iraq on Sunday and Ankara appealed to Iran to stop the rebels fleeing to safety on the fifth day of a major cross-border operation.

F-16 jets bombed rebel positions in the Iraqi mountains, while a column of Turkish tanks moved northeast along the road from Dohuk to the town of Amediye, 70 km (45 miles) away, in what appeared to be preparations for a second prong of attack.

Witnesses saw 10 tanks and armoured cars at the tail of the column passing through the town of Suara Tuka early on Sunday, but local sources said around 100 tanks had passed in the direction of Bamarny and the Matin mountain, west of Amediye.

In Ankara, the Iranian charge d'affaires was called to the foreign ministry and asked for Tehran's support in preventing the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels from escaping Iraq for the safety of the Iran border.

"The charge d'affaires was also told we expected the Iranian security forces to take precautionary measures against elements able to provide support for the PKK from Iranian territory," foreign ministry spokesman Omer Akbel said in a statement.

State-run Anatolian news agency quoted sources at military headquarters as saying 998 rebels had been killed and 141 captured in fighting with troops by Sunday evening. Clashes were intensifying in the regions of Zap and Sinaht near the border.
The military sources gave no details of troop casualties, but on Saturday they said 12 soldiers had been killed.

Journalists have been barred from the region by Turkish troops and their Iraqi Kurdish allies, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP). Communications were blocked, making independent confirmation of the reports impossible.

Pro-Kurdish MED-TV said more than 30 Turkish soldiers had been killed in fighting with the rebels. It made no mention of PKK casualties in northern Iraq, but said one guerrilla had been killed in clashes with soldiers in eastern Turkey, in which 15 troops had died.

The channel said in a written statement the rebels had shot down two army helicopters on Sunday in the triangle of land between Zap, Avasin and Metin. A day earlier it said another helicopter had been downed in the region.
Military headquarters said on Sunday an army helicopter had crashed in northern Iraq after a "technical fault" during the cross-border operation, killing two pilots.
Western capitals and the United Nations have criticised the operation and urged Ankara to withdraw the troops and expressed worry for the safety of civilians.
In Baghdad, Iraq's U.N. coordinator expressed concern over the incursion, saying it might block implementation of Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the world body.
"We are concerned about this development since it may produce an even more volatile security situation in the north, U.N. coordinator Staffan de Mistura told Reuters.
Baghdad has condemned the move as a violation of territorial integrity and a breach of international law.
Ankara said the operation was launched in response to a call from the KDP and was aimed at protecting civilians from a possible "massacre" by the PKK.
"The operation will continue until the terrorist groups in the area are rendered ineffective and the area is controlled by (KDP leader Massoud) Barzani's forces," Akbel said.

The KDP has been generally in charge of the border areas of northern Iraq, while a rival Kurdish group has control further south of the region, set up as an autonomous Kurdish zone by the West following the 1991 Gulf War.

KDP forces, who have in the past objected to Turkey's incursions into Iraq, have been seen working with Turkish forces and they are keeping a tight watch on journalists in the area, helping bar them from the zone and curbing communications.
"We will not allow you to travel for political reasons," Shawkat Barmarni, a KDP official in Dohuk, told a reporter.
